lessons.title: Preparing the Opening: Cleaning and Repairing
lessons.body: Before you install any aluminum window or door, the opening must be clean, square, and structurally sound. Start by removing all debris: old mortar, wood chunks, nails, and dust. Use a wire brush and a hammer to chip away loose material. For concrete or block walls, check for cracks wider than 2mm. Fill these with a non-shrink repair mortar, such as SikaRep or a 1:3 cement-sand mix with a bonding agent. Let it cure for at least 24 hours. If the opening is out of square by more than 5mm, you must correct it. Measure diagonals: they should be equal within 3mm. If not, grind or chip high spots, or apply a leveling render. For brick walls, replace any broken bricks. For wood frame openings, check for rot; replace soft wood with treated timber. Ensure the sill is sloped outward at least 5 degrees to shed water. In hot climates, this prevents water pooling that can lead to mold. Also, check that the opening is the correct size: the frame should fit with a 10-15mm gap all around for expansion and sealing. If the gap is too small, the frame may buckle in heat; if too large, sealing becomes difficult. Clean the surfaces where sealant will bond: they must be free of oil, dust, and loose particles. Use a vacuum or a damp cloth. Finally, prime porous surfaces like concrete and brick with a suitable primer to improve adhesion. This preparation step is criticalâpoor preparation leads to leaks, drafts, and callbacks. Spend the time now to save hours later.

lessons.title: Setting Frames Level and Plumb
lessons.body: Setting frames level and plumb is the most important step for smooth operation and weathertightness. You need a spirit level (at least 600mm long), a plumb bob or laser level, and packers (plastic shims). Start by placing the frame into the opening. Use wooden wedges or plastic packers at the corners and at the midpoint of each side. Do not use stones or wood scraps that can rot. Check level on the sill: place the level on the bottom frame. Adjust packers until the bubble is centered. Then check plumb on each side: hold the level vertically against the jamb. Adjust packers until plumb. Check the head (top) for level. Now check the diagonals: measure from top-left corner to bottom-right, then top-right to bottom-left. They must be equal within 2mm. If not, adjust packers until they match. This ensures the frame is square. For doors, also check that the threshold is level and that the frame is not twisted. Use a string line across the face of the frame to check for twist. In hot climates, aluminum expands; leave a 5mm gap at the top and sides for expansion. Do not over-pack: packers should be snug but not forcing the frame out of shape. Once level and plumb, secure the frame temporarily with screws or nails through the packers into the wall. Re-check all measurements. A common mistake is to fix the frame before checking diagonals. Always check and re-check. If the frame is not level and plumb, the windows will not close properly, and water will leak. Take your timeâthis step sets the foundation for the entire installation.

lessons.title: Fixing Frames to Block, Brick, and Concrete Walls
lessons.body: The method of fixing depends on the wall material. For block and brick walls, use masonry screws or expansion anchors. Drill holes through the frame into the wall using a hammer drill and a bit slightly smaller than the screw. For concrete, use concrete anchors or wedge bolts. Space fixings at maximum 600mm apart, and within 150mm of each corner. For windows, fix through the sides and top; for doors, also fix through the bottom (threshold) if it is a fixed frame. Do not fix through the drainage holes or the weatherstripping. Use stainless steel screws to avoid rust. Pre-drill the aluminum frame to prevent cracking. For brick, avoid fixing into mortar joints; fix into the brick itself. For block, if the block is hollow, use toggle bolts or chemical anchors. In hot climates, use plastic isolation tape between the aluminum frame and steel or concrete to prevent galvanic corrosion. After fixing, check that the frame is still level and plumb. If you overtighten, you can distort the frame. Tighten screws snugly, then check operation of the window or door. If it binds, loosen and adjust. For large openings, fix the mullions (vertical dividers) securely. Always follow the manufacturer's instructions for fixing positions. A common error is to fix only at the corners, causing the frame to bow. Fix at regular intervals. After fixing, cut off any protruding packers flush with the frame. Then proceed to sealing. Remember: the fixings hold the frame in place, but the sealant provides the weather seal. Both are essential.

lessons.title: Sealing Gaps with Expanding Foam and Sealant
lessons.body: Sealing is what keeps water, air, and insects out. Use low-expansion polyurethane foam for gaps wider than 10mm. Shake the can well, then inject foam into the gap, filling about 50% because it expands. Do not overfill, or it will bow the frame. Let it cure for at least 1 hour (depending on humidity). Trim excess foam with a knife after it is fully cured. For gaps smaller than 10mm, use a high-quality silicone or polyurethane sealant. Clean the surfaces first: they must be dry, dust-free, and oil-free. Use a backing rod (foam rod) for deep gaps to control sealant depth and save material. Apply sealant with a caulking gun at a 45-degree angle, pushing the sealant ahead of the nozzle. Tool the sealant with a spatula or your finger dipped in soapy water to smooth it and ensure good adhesion. In hot climates, choose a sealant that can withstand high temperatures and UV exposure, such as neutral-cure silicone or polyurethane. Do not use acrylic sealant outdoors. Seal both inside and outside. On the outside, ensure a continuous seal around the entire frame. Pay special attention to the sill: seal the ends and the back of the sill to prevent water ingress. For doors, seal the threshold and sides. After sealing, check for gaps by shining a light from inside at night. If you see light, re-seal. Allow sealant to cure for 24 hours before exposing to water. Proper sealing prevents drafts, water damage, and mold, which are common problems in African climates with heavy rains and intense sun.

lessons.title: Installing Windows and Doors in Hot Climates
lessons.body: Hot climates present unique challenges: extreme heat, intense UV, and heavy rains. Aluminum expands significantly in heatâabout 1mm per meter for a 50Â°C temperature change. So, always leave expansion gaps: 5mm at the top and sides for windows, and 10mm for large doors. Never fix frames rigidly at both ends; allow one end to slide. Use thermal breaks if possible: these are plastic separators between the inner and outer aluminum, reducing heat transfer. For windows, consider low-E glass or tinted glass to reduce solar gain. Install windows with the drainage holes facing outward and unobstructed. In hot climates, rain can be torrential; ensure the sill has a slope of at least 5 degrees and a drip groove. Use wide overhangs or awnings if possible to protect the sealant from direct sun and rain. Sealant degrades faster under UV; choose a UV-resistant sealant and inspect annually. For doors, install with a raised threshold to prevent water ingress during heavy rain. Use weatherstripping that can withstand high temperatures, such as silicone or EPDM. Avoid PVC weatherstripping, which can become brittle. In dusty areas, use brush seals in addition to rubber seals. During installation, work in the cooler parts of the day to avoid heat stress and to prevent sealant from skinning too fast. If the frame is in direct sun, cool it with water before applying sealant. After installation, check that windows and doors operate freely; heat expansion may cause binding if gaps are insufficient. Regular maintenance: lubricate hinges and locks with a silicone spray every 6 months. Following these practices ensures your installation lasts in harsh African conditions.

lessons.title: Final Adjustments and Testing Operation
lessons.body: After installation and sealing, you must test and adjust. Open and close each window and door several times. They should operate smoothly with one hand. If they stick, check the hinges and rollers. For sliding windows, adjust the rollers using a screwdriver: turn the adjustment screw clockwise to raise the sash, counterclockwise to lower. For casement windows, adjust the friction stays or hinges. For doors, adjust the hinges: loosen the screws slightly, tap the hinge to align, then retighten. Check the lock: it should engage easily without forcing. If the lock is misaligned, adjust the strike plate or the frame. Check the drainage: pour a cup of water into the window track; it should drain out the weep holes quickly. If not, clear the holes with a wire. Check the seal: close the window and run your hand around the edges to feel for drafts. At night, shine a light from inside and look for gaps outside. If you find gaps, re-seal. For doors, check the threshold seal: it should touch the floor evenly. Adjust if needed. Also check that all screws are tight and that packers are trimmed. Clean the glass and frames with a soft cloth and mild soap. Do not use abrasive cleaners. Finally, demonstrate operation to the client: show them how to open, close, lock, and clean. Provide a maintenance schedule: lubricate moving parts every 6 months, check sealant annually, and clean drainage holes. A well-installed and adjusted window or door will last for decades and keep your client happy.

quiz.q: What is the maximum allowable difference in diagonal measurements when preparing an opening?
quiz.explanation: Diagonals should be equal within 3mm to ensure the opening is square.

quiz.q: Why should the sill be sloped outward?
options: A) To make it look better
B) To shed water and prevent pooling
quiz.explanation: A slope of at least 5 degrees ensures water drains away, preventing mold and water damage.

quiz.q: What is the recommended gap around a frame for expansion and sealing?
quiz.explanation: A 10-15mm gap allows for thermal expansion and provides space for sealant.

quiz.q: Which tool is essential for checking if a frame is level?
quiz.explanation: A spirit level is used to check both level and plumb.

quiz.q: What should you use to pack the frame during installation?
quiz.explanation: Plastic shims are durable, won't rot, and provide precise adjustment.

quiz.q: When checking plumb, where do you hold the level?
quiz.explanation: Plumb is checked vertically against the side jamb.

quiz.q: What is the maximum spacing for fixings in block or brick walls?
quiz.explanation: Fixings should be spaced no more than 600mm apart, and within 150mm of corners.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid fixing into mortar joints in brick walls?
options: B) Mortar is weaker than brick
quiz.explanation: Mortar joints are weaker and may not hold fixings securely.

quiz.q: What type of screw should be used for fixing aluminum frames?
quiz.explanation: Stainless steel screws resist rust and corrosion.

quiz.q: What should be used between aluminum and steel to prevent galvanic corrosion?
quiz.explanation: Plastic tape acts as a dielectric barrier to prevent corrosion.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of low-expansion foam?
options: A) To fill gaps wider than 10mm
B) To fill gaps smaller than 10mm
quiz.explanation: Low-expansion foam is used for gaps wider than 10mm to avoid bowing the frame.

quiz.q: How full should you fill a gap with expanding foam?
quiz.explanation: Foam expands, so filling 50% prevents over-expansion and frame distortion.

quiz.q: What is a backing rod used for?
quiz.explanation: Backing rod limits sealant depth, saving material and ensuring proper curing.

quiz.q: Which sealant is best for hot climates?
quiz.explanation: Polyurethane sealant withstands high temperatures and UV better than acrylic or latex.

quiz.q: How long should you wait before exposing sealant to water?
quiz.explanation: Most sealants require 24 hours to cure before water exposure.

quiz.q: What is the recommended expansion gap for large doors in hot climates?
quiz.explanation: Large doors need a 10mm gap to accommodate thermal expansion.

quiz.q: What is a thermal break in aluminum frames?
quiz.explanation: Thermal breaks are plastic separators that reduce heat transfer through the frame.

quiz.q: Why should drainage holes face outward?
quiz.explanation: Drainage holes allow water that enters the track to escape outside.

quiz.q: What type of weatherstripping is best for hot climates?
quiz.explanation: EPDM withstands high temperatures and UV better than PVC or felt.

quiz.q: How often should you lubricate hinges and locks?
quiz.explanation: Regular lubrication every 6 months keeps moving parts functioning smoothly.

quiz.q: What should you do if a sliding window sticks?
quiz.explanation: Adjusting the rollers raises or lowers the sash to improve operation.

quiz.q: How can you check for drafts around a closed window?
options: B) Run your hand around edges
quiz.explanation: A candle flame flickers, and your hand can feel air movement.

quiz.q: What should you pour into a window track to test drainage?
quiz.explanation: Water should drain out quickly through weep holes.

quiz.q: What is the correct way to clean aluminum frames?
quiz.explanation: Mild soap and water clean without damaging the finish.

quiz.q: What should you demonstrate to the client after installation?
options: B) How to operate and maintain
quiz.explanation: Clients should know how to open, close, lock, and maintain their windows and doors.

quiz.q: Why is it important to check diagonals after fixing?
quiz.explanation: Equal diagonals confirm the frame is square, preventing operation issues.

quiz.q: What can happen if you over-tighten fixing screws?
quiz.explanation: Over-tightening can bow the frame, causing windows to stick.

quiz.q: What is the minimum cure time for non-shrink repair mortar before installing a frame?
quiz.explanation: Repair mortar must cure for at least 24 hours to gain strength.

quiz.q: What should you use to clean surfaces before applying sealant?
quiz.explanation: Surfaces must be dry, dust-free, and oil-free; a damp cloth removes dust.

quiz.q: What is the recommended slope for a sill?
quiz.explanation: A 5-degree slope ensures proper water drainage.
